text:
emily: Support FYI — multiple hosted customers reporting sudden 503s and long tail timeouts starting ~09:35 UTC. Patterns show upstream infer-worker exit (SIGABRT) followed by container restart; customers see ~2-4% error spike. Anyone oncall?

michael: I'm oncall, looking now. Do we have request_ids / sample payloads? Which model and route?

sre_bot: alert: infer-runner-03 terminated (signal 6) at 09:35:12 UTC. Crash loop detected, restart_count=5.

emily: Two customer request ids: req-0a1b2c (ACME Corp), req-9f8e7d (BetaApps). Both hit /v1/respond with tool-calls and long context (~90k chars). Model: redwood-v3-large-quant. Minimal stderr excerpt below.

emily: ```
[stderr] 2026-03-16T09:35:12.452Z infer-runner: caught signal 6 (SIGABRT)
[stderr] 2026-03-16T09:35:12.453Z runtime: abort: cuda out of memory during kv_prefetch
[stdout] 2026-03-16T09:35:12.460Z watchdog: restarting container (backoff 2s)
```

nathan: Confirmed GPU OOM (nvml reports memory spike) immediately prior to abort, then a segfault in native runtime. Looks like kvcache growth during toolcall + dynbatch expansion.

jess: We merged a dynbatch tuning yesterday (2026-03-15 22:10 UTC) that increases max_batch_size for speed; rolling that back now as a mitigation. :warning:

infra_oncall: Rolling back dynbatch tweak on prod canary. Also increasing restart backoff and pod memory limit as a short-term band-aid. Will monitor error rate.

alex: Immediate routing mitigation: add fallback to redwood-v3-medium-quant for requests over 64k chars and set max_batch_size=8 for affected routes. Pushing policy patch to gateway.

michael: Drafted a support reply to customers asking for full request payload (sanitized) and counts of retries. Notifying CS and billing — no billing anomalies yet but customers saw repeated 503s.

emily: Customers replied — they saw 3 retries before success, and they included an example prompt (stripped) that includes nested tool calls and a 120k token-ish context.

jess: After rollback + routing fallback, initial metrics: error rate dropped from 3.1% -> 0.5% at p95 over the last 4m. Still investigating root cause for kvcache leak/growth.

nathan: Repro steps we used locally: set KV_PREFETCH=1 and run a long toolcall payload against redwood-v3-large-quant with dynbatch enabled. Example: 

```bash
export KV_PREFETCH=1
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-infer.test/v1/respond -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -d @large_toolcall_payload.json
# observe nvml stats: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -d 1
```

alex: For the postmortem: check allocator behaviour for quantized kernels, the model swap path when kvcache expands, and the watchdog restart/backoff interplay. Also add a canary gate for dynbatch parameter changes.

infra_oncall: I've collected heap dumps, nvml logs, and crash stacks from the affected nodes and uploaded to /mnt/incident-artifacts/7259876543/.

michael: Flagging this for a P1 RCA timeline. CS updated customers; will keep channel open until RCA posted.

emily: Thanks — closing the immediate support loop with customers (they accepted fallback to medium-quant). Leaving thread for follow-up RCA updates. :white_check_mark:
